title: The progression of impiety and the rejection of Providence
english: Regarding what concerns the calling of the Gentiles. The 'Only One' should not be troubled, for the Son cannot do anything contrary to the Father, unless he sees the Father doing it; for whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does. For the 'Only One' and such things taken regarding divinity declare a Father and a Son, as it is presented from the prophet; for it is said to the Father: 'And the Sabaean men shall pass over high upon you and shall worship you and shall pray to you, that what is in you is God and is not God except you; for you are God, and not to be feared, God of Israel, Savior' (Ps 72:1,2). Who is the glory whose name is blessed, who having arrived has made glorious and honorable those from the worthless and gloryless who are the repentant men? It is possible to call his glory and he did not receive an unsung death for the sake of the salvation of the world; for Jesus was not yet glorified, and the Jesus whom we see being humbled through the suffering of death is being crowned with glory and honor.

If indeed his glory is that which his name is blessed for unto the age, concerning which Paul writes: 'Not worthy are the sufferings of the present time compared to the glory that is about to be revealed to us, stand fast' (Rom 8:18). For especially this and the proclamation concerning it we find to be eternally hymned, as Peter said; thus says the witness of his sufferings and of the glory about to be revealed: 'And a companion of that glory' (2 Pet 1:11). And Israel seeing God is interpreted. Therefore also, those not seeing him, they perceive what is good (Ps 72:6b-9). For indeed, although it provides something dark and unpleasant to men, they perceive how it also works advantageously toward salvation, and their steps are not shaken having crossed over and having advanced. Since those about whom the word is, are held not by practical wickedness alone but also by impiety, followingly they are clothed in injustice.

And [there is] the moral wickedness according to the soul, and with this impiety, they think impiously concerning all dogmas. And also to say that their injustice will come forth as from a cloud; then, when it comes forth, the sin is practically fulfilled, no longer remaining only in the thoughts. It has passed into a disposition of the heart.

Having previously disposed themselves according to wickedness, they not only established the evil to themselves but also desired to be harmful to others. Then, after passing into a disposition of wickedness, having thought in malice, they spoke deceitfully as if of good things. They were lifted up, he says, as if to speak even against God, slandering His justice, His creation, and His providence; such as are those who, at the time of the stars, having set their preconceptions, and those who, making the heavens and the creation [themselves] instead of the Creator, lift up their mouth to heaven. They were torn apart, rather they were consumed, as if their tongue had passed through the earth against the Most High, so that all who hear might know what vain and impious things are being philosophized against God and His providence (Ps 72:10).

Of the impious boasting loudly (Ps 72:10), the people of God calls as a starting point for a good return, desiring to enjoy the contemplations of the light of day. And the 'Here' [referring to] the one saying this is God, such as what was said to Moses: 'And you shall stand with me' (Ex 33:33).

Those wanting to cast out providence and injustice, having spoken toward the height (Ps 72:11-13), bring forth such words; how can one know God through human things? For does [the intellect] not have a sensory, organic power? For his understanding does not receive the forms of the seen and the heard, so that, having known, he might also know providential and royal things as he wishes? And having said before, 'How will God be known?', they confess to knowing God, but they are ignorant of the manner of knowing.
